summary: An independent architectural experiment separating prepared boundary context from late LOCK permission. This document specifies a conditional design and its proof obligations; it adds no RTL, pin wiring, timing exception or implementation result.

public_base.meaning: Native LOCK ownership and release are not implemented by this public baseline. The proposed controller and event producers below are design targets, not descriptions of existing public RTL.
public_base.independence: No unpublished implementation, captures, firmware, private receipt or previous experimental branch is imported. Previous local architectural studies motivate questions, but do not provide validation evidence in this fork.

design_principle: SIMPLICITY: this is 80's era hardware — nothing on the die is wasted. Complex or confusing observed behavior is likely simple systems interacting in ways not yet understood. A large fitted table, a many-cased rule, or a per-opcode special case is a signal of misunderstanding, not a deliverable.

proposed_profile.save_state: inactive in the first proposed integration scope
proposed_profile.qualification: This is a new, explicit integration profile. A CE opportunity may still be withheld by the existing transaction or yield protocol. LOCK preparation must not add a CPU wait or suppress an otherwise accepted CE.
proposed_profile.not_portable: The public core permits adjacent CE/CE_HALF phases in multiplexed mode and imposes no five-slot spacing requirement on demultiplexed CE. This profile does not replace that portable contract or the multiplexed rig.
proposed_profile.half_phase: Five 20 ns ticks do not provide an exact 50 ns midpoint using only rising fabric edges. No multiplexed half-phase schedule is asserted here.
proposed_profile.clock_policy: No automatic 100 MHz clock proposal, PLL change or multicycle exception follows from these arithmetic values. Launch, capture, enable and stability must be proved for each actual endpoint.

target: Actual BUSLOCK pin at every declared observable deadline
Valid FIRST acquisition with acquisition priority over release
Actual first and second INTA T1 behavior
Reset and, in a later scope, owned and unrelated save-state priorities
proposed_observable_contract.auxiliary_admission: Universal equality of an auxiliary admission signal outside its sensitive domain is not the architectural target. Equal pin samples alone are also insufficient if a hidden hold update differs.

controller_law_to_validate.symbols: A = valid acquisition; H = prefix ownership hold; H1 = INTA-pair hold; G = candidate grant; I = actual INTA low arm.
controller_law_to_validate.inta_low: actual_INTA_T1 ? !H1 : H1; actual_INTA_T1 means an active INTA transaction in T1, never an ordinary memory/I/O T1 or an INTA issue preview.
controller_law_to_validate.H_normal_update: On an accepted CE: A sets H; otherwise G clears H; otherwise H is retained.
controller_law_to_validate.H1_normal_update: Toggle only on the specified actual INTA T1 exit event, not on an issue preview or an address-parity hint.
controller_law_to_validate.reset: Force pin HIGH immediately and clear normal holds at the actual reset sampling edge.
controller_law_to_validate.future_save_state: Owned hold restore must have explicitly defined priority over normal reset/CE updates; unrelated save-state inhibits normal events. This policy is not implemented or validated here.

proposed_observable_contract.binary_masking_obligation: With equal current holds, acquisition and INTA arm, pin sensitivity to G requires !reset && H && !A && !I. Hold-update sensitivity requires !save_state_write && !reset && accepted_CE && H && !A. These Boolean conditions do not prove four-state behavior or silicon timing.
proposed_observable_contract.first_use: The first observable use can be a SYS edge before the next CPU CE. A context completed just before the next CE is not automatically early enough.

candidate_structure.name: warm context banks, ownership epoch and late grant
candidate_structure.scope: A separate proposed LOCK unit; the architectural EU/BIU and all non-LOCK outputs remain unchanged unless a later reviewed design explicitly expands scope.
candidate_structure.warm_bank_hypothesis: Prepare six possible source-ROM control contexts for hold, sequential advance, local jump, far redirect, entry and IRQ entry in the preceding CPU window. A late actual selector chooses a prepared bank. Availability, completeness and selection timing are unproved; naming six banks does not cover every late ENTRY or successor path.
candidate_structure.storage_subtotal_equation: 6 * 16 warm-bank bits + 16 active-context bits + 8 control bits = 120 proposed transient bits.
candidate_structure.cost_limits: This subtotal excludes projection payload, bypass state, any additional bank/tag requirements and the two proposed ownership holds. Total FF/ALM cost is unknown; no fitter count or speed prediction is claimed.
candidate_structure.single_inflight_epoch: A one-bit epoch is conditional on a single in-flight context and complete cancellation before reuse. More outstanding work requires a proved tag width and wrap policy.
candidate_structure.forbidden_hidden_dependency: The late grant must not call the full effective-state decoder, read final st_n/global prospective resources as a convenience, or duplicate STEP/unroll in a new file. A fallback to the original long combinational cone would retain that timing path and does not implement this partition.

stable_intent_and_late_results.stable_only_after_source_proof: ROM pattern controls and destination intents can be banked only when their descriptor origin and selector are known. A late branch selector is not itself a stable field.
stable_intent_and_late_results.writes_opr: Store destination intent only. Actual qualification still depends on blocked state, required Q availability, operand kinds and SIGMA/suppression after the original ordered writers.
stable_intent_and_late_results.write_add: Store raw write kind only. The actual zero/one/two write debt depends on writeback qualification, suppression and address parity after transfers. Split parity must not be frozen without a stability proof.
stable_intent_and_late_results.early_E: A dynamic early-E qualification is not identical to a ROM E bit and must have its own proved producer or late bypass.
stable_intent_and_late_results.frame_release: Store the structural COUNT-to-OPR pattern; actual boundary, F, free/eval and retirement qualifications remain live.
stable_intent_and_late_results.successor_valid: A local ordered acceptance/consumption record must prove whether the window has closed. Reading final global opcode-valid merely under a different name does not establish separation.
stable_intent_and_late_results.late_inputs: Q maturity/consumption, read completion, READY qualification, OPR/debt changes, PSW read-edge override, IRQ/NMI recognition, slot/access availability and split completion remain legal late inputs. They must not be frozen to manufacture pipeline slack.
stable_intent_and_late_results.context_changing_late_input: If a late input changes the context kind or ordered resources rather than permission alone, an exact short bypass is required. Marking the context dirty cannot complete several stages instantaneously. Such a bypass is not established yet.

five_slot_schedule.work: Launch ownership/epoch and source-bound preparation after accepted CE0. Any sensitive output before P1 requires a context already prepared in the previous CPU window.
five_slot_schedule.publication: Acquisition, reset and actual INTA must retain their own original deadlines.

five_slot_schedule.work: Predecode proven source-ROM alternatives into warm contexts; preserve actual late branch selection.
five_slot_schedule.unproved: The source-to-bank path and complete branch population.

five_slot_schedule.work: Project only source-local ordered completion, OPR, PSW and debt events with their original priority.
five_slot_schedule.unproved: A complete projection that does not reproduce the execution dispatcher.

five_slot_schedule.work: Resolve the prepared window and publish a combinational late grant from live permissions.
five_slot_schedule.deadline: A capture at CE100 that consumes a prior SYS sampler taken at 80 ns requires the pin to be stable before the 80 ns edge. A new register first written at 80 ns does not supply that old-value sample.

five_slot_schedule.work: Keep late permission live for actual consumers and update ownership holds only at the accepted CE100.
five_slot_schedule.qualification: A newly specified consumer sampling directly at CE100 could have a different deadline. That does not preserve earlier pin transitions or silently replace an existing sampler contract.

event_and_epoch_policy.launch: From a proved original handover and its ordered source fields, not simply from E or the final effective state.
event_and_epoch_policy.retain: A dry but eligible boundary remains a recognition window. The instruction epoch spans an entire REP block; HALT retains ownership during standby.
event_and_epoch_policy.cancel: Cancel on the actual successor acceptance or recognition that closes the window, and on invalidating reset/restore/profile changes. A pre-popped successor may close a window in the same evaluation in which it opened.
event_and_epoch_policy.startup: Before the first sensitive pin deadline there must be a valid selected context for the current epoch. There is no unproved warm-up grace period with H already restored or acquired.
event_and_epoch_policy.reset: Immediate pin override is independent of the pipeline; cancel all pending contexts and old tags. Define the first valid post-reset sample explicitly.
event_and_epoch_policy.save_state_pending_scope: The first proposed profile ties save-state inactive. A later profile must restore transient state or prove flush/relaunch before the first observable use, including owned and unrelated writes and reset priority. No current portable save-state claim is made.
event_and_epoch_policy.pause_or_yield: CPU state may pause, but live inputs and combinational pin permission can still change. Do not stop the grant merely because CE is absent.
event_and_epoch_policy.mode_or_divisor_change: Require an explicit cancel/restart and first-valid-sample protocol; do not reuse a prepared context across a changed schedule.

late_grant_outline: Select a valid, matching-epoch context whose birth and cancellation are source-proved.
ROW requires ordered pending/block/Q/pre-wait/slot/retirement checks; permission is recognition or an allowed ripe FIRST when no flush prevents the pop.
Deferred and released-tail windows require their own delivery/emission and retirement checks; recognition remains possible with dry Q.
An opcode window requires actual boundary arming; a prefix loop must not acquire a fabricated instruction boundary.
Compute grant from that context and live permission. Preserve acquisition priority and actual INTA independently.
This outline is not an executable producer: the source-bound window and local resource network remain undefined.
validity_miss: An isolated shadow must fail and retain the first miss. Hardware must not silently keep LOCK low, add a CPU wait, use an old epoch or fall back to the long cone. A correct miss policy or proof of no miss is required before candidate pin wiring.
outputs_other_than_LOCK: No q_pop, EU post, queue flush, CE acceptance, AD/status or other bus output may be changed merely to make the LOCK pipeline work. Any dependency on those unchanged outputs must be source-accounted. A downstream bridge/IPC redesign is an option for a separate contract, not an existing fact.

bounded_milestones.deliverable: Exact birth/select/cancel events, ordered local late-write producers, removed dependency rails and the first observable deadline. Resolve ENTRY, last-Q, same-evaluation successor closure and previous-window preparation without a copied dispatcher.
bounded_milestones.stop: No prototype if this partition or an explicitly approved new temporal contract is missing.

bounded_milestones.deliverable: A preregistered, reviewed prototype leaving the architectural core and pin oracle unchanged. Check actual pin plus both holds, acquisition and INTA at all sensitive phases; retain misses and failures.
Declared source-bound functional witnesses and independent native evidence appropriate to the claimed integration. Finite model equivalence is engineering evidence, not silicon validation.

An exact-tree artifact-backed physical result under reviewed constraints. Preserve the existing G6 requirement of Fmax >= 32 MHz, worst setup > 0 and setup/hold TNS = 0; do not relax it because CPU opportunities are 10 MHz. Separately close the proposed 50 MHz profile against its 20 ns applicable launch/capture endpoints and all setup/hold requirements, with any exceptions justified by verified source enables and actual endpoint collections. Passing G6 at 32 MHz alone does not validate this 50 MHz profile; 100 ns CPU spacing is not universal timing slack.

preregisterable_falsifiers: First early sensitive handover with H=1, A=0 and no INTA masking, before the new context finishes
Last operand Q changes binding or ordered resources during preparation
Dry Q with IRQ/NMI becoming eligible, and flush with recognition but no pop
Last-tick read response/READY and PSW read-edge override
Second split-write half and pairing while a slot wait remains
Reset/startup with a pending context; later owned/unrelated save-state with restored ownership
Wrong epoch, omitted capture or selector with an original-sensitive anchor before the expected private rejection
Adjacent portable CE/half phases against any attempted universal five-slot claim
source_anchors_in_public_base: hdl/rtl/ucore/v30_core.sv:198-270: CE/CE_HALF contract and demultiplexed qualification

claims.documented_by_public_source: Public BUSLOCK stub, enable contract and sampler/input-register structure only.
claims.hypothetical: Context banks, stage schedule, controller law, epochs, bypasses and storage subtotal.
claims.not_claimed: RTL implementation, functional pass, native waveform fidelity, timing closure, speed improvement, portable compatibility or complete save-state support.
